import os
import tempfile
import pytest

# Import the public API that is available in the codebase
from doorstop.core import tree as tree_module
from doorstop.core import document as document_module
from doorstop.core import importer as importer_module
from doorstop.core import item as item_module


# Helper to create a temporary document tree and a document
def create_temp_document(prefix="DOC"):
    # Create an empty tree
    t = tree_module.Tree.from_list([])
    # Create a temporary directory to hold the document
    tmp_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    # Create a new document in the tree
    doc = document_module.Document.new(
        t, tmp_dir, t.root, prefix, parent=None
    )
    return t, doc, tmp_dir


def test_U02_4__UML_Testing___TC_001_store_requirement():
    """
    Test that a requirement can be stored successfully.
    """
    # Arrange
    t, doc, _ = create_temp_document("REQDOC")
    # Act: add an item with the requirement text
    item = importer_module.add_item(
        prefix=doc.prefix,
        uid="1",
        attrs={"text": "Requirement text"},
        document=doc,
    )
    # Assert: the item is stored and its text matches the input
    assert isinstance(item, item_module.Item)
    assert item.text == "Requirement text"

def test_U02_4__UML_Testing___TC_004_scale_to_large_requirements():
    """
    Test that the system can handle a large number of requirements without errors.
    """
    # Arrange
    t, doc, _ = create_temp_document("BIGDOC")
    # Act: create a large number of items
    num_items = 1000  # adjust as needed for the test environment
    for i in range(1, num_items + 1):
        importer_module.add_item(
            prefix=doc.prefix,
            uid=str(i),
            attrs={"text": f"Requirement {i}"},
            document=doc,
        )
    # Assert: all items are present
    assert len(doc.items) == num_items
    # Optionally, check that the tree contains the document
    assert doc in t
